sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento delle tensioni geopolitiche tra USA e Iran, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è sopra 18, il DXY è stabile e il TLT è in calo. Le borse asiatiche sono state deboli, con il Nikkei in calo dell'1,23%.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to rising geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran, negatively impacting equity markets and increasing demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX is above 18, the DXY is stable, and TLT is down. Asian markets were weak, with Nikkei down 1.23%.

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari sono stati deboli oggi, con il S&P 500 in calo dello 0,67% e il Nikkei in calo dell'1,23%. Il DXY è stabile a 99,43 e il VIX è sopra 18. Il prezzo del petrolio è sceso dell'1,43% a $109,69. Le borse europee sono deboli, con lo STOXX 600 in aumento dello 0,23%.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets were weak today, with the S&P 500 down 0.67% and Nikkei down 1.23%. The DXY is stable at 99.43 and VIX is above 18. Oil prices fell 1.43% to $109.69. European markets are weak, with STOXX 600 up 0.23%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.23%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.18%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dello 0.67%, il VIX è sceso dello 0.22% a 18.02 Il Dollar Index è salito dello 0.14% a 99.43 L'oro è sceso dello 0.47% a $4485.2 l'oncia. Il petrolio Brent è in calo dell'1.43% a $109.69 I rendimenti dei titoli di stato americani sono in aumento, con il US 10Y Yield in salita dello 0.95% a 4.66%. I BTP 10Y italiani sono stabili al 3.73%.

L'inflazione nel Regno Unito è scesa al 2.8% ad aprile, nonostante lo shock energetico in Medio Oriente. Questo dato potrebbe influenzare la politica monetaria della Banca d'Inghilterra. La crisi energetica in Medio Oriente sta spingendo India e Sud-Est asiatico a tornare verso il carbone.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantasettemila dollari, con una variazione del +0,37%. I flussi ETF hanno registrato una significativa uscita di 648,6 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dichiarazioni dei senatori statunitensi riguardo alle potenzialità di guerra in Iran. Inoltre, la senatrice Elizabeth Warren ha accusato un regolatore statunitense di aver approvato banche crypto non qualificate. 
  Tra le altre criptovalute, Ethereum è pressoché invariato a duemilacentotrentatre dollari, con un calo dell'0,21%. Solana scende dello 0,51% a ottantaquattro dollari e novantatre centesimi. BNB invece registra un leggero aumento dello 0,15%, arrivando a seicentoquarantadue dollari. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 27, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita. Per approfondire, trovate gli articoli sulla nostra piattaforma nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

The Nikkei closed down 1.23%, Shanghai down 0.18%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed down 0.67%, the VIX fell 0.22% to 18.02 The Dollar Index rose 0.14% to 99.43 Gold fell 0.47% to $4,485.2 an ounce. Brent crude oil is down 1.43% to $109.69 US Treasury yields are rising, with the US 10Y Yield up 0.95% to 4.66%. Italian BTPs 10Y are stable at 3.73%.

UK inflation fell to 2.8% in April, despite the energy shock in the Middle East. This data could influence the Bank of England's monetary policy. The energy crisis in the Middle East is pushing India and Southeast Asia to turn back to coal.

No major macroeconomic data releases today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above seventy-seven thousand dollars, with a change of +0.37%. ETF flows have recorded a significant outflow of $648.6 million. This movement could be influenced by recent statements from US senators regarding the potential for war in Iran. Furthermore, Senator Elizabeth Warren accused a US regulator of approving unqualified crypto banks.

Among other cryptocurrencies, Ethereum is essentially flat at $2,133, down 0.21%. Solana falls 0.51% to $84.93 BNB instead records a slight increase of 0.15%, reaching $642 

The Fear & Greed Index is at 27, in Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors.

We are waiting for economic data releases. For more details, find the articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.title: Trump’s approach to Taiwan could jeopardize its future. Indo-Pacific allies are taking note
articles.snippet: Trump’s approach to Taiwan could jeopardize its future. Indo-Pacific allies are taking note Expert comment LToremark 19 May 2026 Trump’s comments on Taiwan after his meeting with Xi and an apparent move towards ‘strategic stability’ with China could have consequences for Taiwan’s future and erode trust among US allies. When US President Donald Trump met with China’s President Xi Jinping in Beijing last week, there was concern that he might negotiate the future of Taiwan to strike a deal with China. For Beijing, Taiwan is the most important issue in the US-China bilateral relationship. Xi even warned that if the issue is mishandled, it could trigger ‘clashes and even conflicts’. Reports in the run-up to the meeting suggested that China would seek a change in America’s long-standing position

articles.title: The Navy Needs Precise Mass and Here Is How to Get There
articles.snippet: Maintaining deterrence in the Indo-Pacific and around the world requires the U.S. Navy to change what it builds and how it fights. Sen. Roger Wicker observed in 2024 that the United States’ approach to fleet design and ship construction is “too small and too old.” The current model of naval power cannot scale at the speed modern war demands. The war with Iran is already exposing the limits. articles.title: Sustainable Economies Will Own the Future
articles.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and the wars in Ukraine and Iran have reframed the issue of sustainability, which is now as much about sovereignty and economic security as it is about planetary health. Countries and companies that fail to recognize this have everything to lose in the coming years.

articles.title: Europe’s EV Sales Surge as Oil Shock Hits Drivers
articles.snippet: Sales of electric vehicles in Europe are on the rise as the Middle East war disruption in oil exports pushes retail fuel prices higher, Reuters reported today, citing data from the industry that showed demand for EVs had gone up by 34% in April. The data comes from 16 markets, Reuters noted in its report, with the figures showing strengthening demand for electric cars in already highly pro-EV markets such as the Netherlands and Denmark, but also from markets such as Italy, where adoption has been slower to pick up.
